code.originalText: Staging laparoscopy result and tumor board recommendation; first cycle of chemoimmunotherapy and specialist palliative care

text.paragraph: Staging laparoscopy result, tumor board recommendation, and first cycle of treatment. [S]

Mr. Sun returns two weeks after the consultation and five days after the staging laparoscopy. At laparoscopy the surgeon found several small nodules on the lining of the abdomen and the omentum, and their biopsy shows adenocarcinoma of the same type. The tumor board met two days later and advised against an operation and for chemoimmunotherapy. He has recovered from the laparoscopy; the port and the small wounds are healing. The ache under his ribs is unchanged at 2 of 10. He said he had expected this, as a physician, but found it hard to hear. He has slept poorly for several nights. He wants to start treatment today if he is fit for it and asked how long treatment might keep him working. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1924-06-01; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin, composed; blood pressure 126/80, pulse 84; weight 60.0 kg; no jaundice
Healing laparoscopy wounds; mass 4 cm below the right costal margin, unchanged; no ascites
Hears a whispered voice in both ears

Right upper quadrant abdominal mass with weight loss: a dull ache under the right ribs and early fullness for about three months, 4 kg weight loss, and a firm, non-tender mass felt 4 cm below the right costal margin; no jaundice, fever, or itching. Ultrasound today: a 6.8 cm solid, heterogeneous mass in liver segments IV and V that cannot be separated from the gallbladder, which contains stones; the rest of the liver is smooth, with no ascites. Multiphase CT, tumor markers, hepatitis serology and medical oncology consultation arranged
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented right upper abdominal mass; superseded by the biopsy diagnosis.

Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder invading the liver: core biopsy of the liver mass shows moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (CK7 positive, CK20 and CDX2 negative), and multiphase CT and MRI show a 7.1 cm mass arising from the gallbladder fundus and invading liver segments IVb and V, with gallstones and two enlarged nodes in the hepatoduodenal ligament; no cirrhosis; alpha-fetoprotein normal, CA 19-9 raised. Clinical T3 N1 before staging laparoscopy (AJCC 8th edition). Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented final illness, described in life as liver cancer and at autopsy as gallbladder adenocarcinoma
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis chosen to fit the documented findings: a mass involving the liver at operation and gallbladder adenocarcinoma at autopsy.

Resolved hepatitis B infection: hepatitis B surface antigen negative, total core antibody positive, surface antibody positive, HBV DNA undetectable; hepatitis C antibody negative. At risk of reactivation during chemotherapy and immunotherapy; monitored
S — Synthetic serology; not a claim that he had hepatitis B in his lifetime. No fetched source mentions hepatitis.

Peritoneal metastases from gallbladder adenocarcinoma: several 3 to 6 mm nodules on the parietal peritoneum and omentum at staging laparoscopy, biopsy positive for adenocarcinoma of the same type; stage IVB (M1), not resectable
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the peritoneal metastases reported at autopsy.

list.item:
Peritoneal metastases from gallbladder adenocarcinoma (C78.6). Peritoneal metastases confirmed by biopsy: stage IVB (any T, any N, M1). Not resectable; treatment aims to control the cancer, relieve symptoms and lengthen life, not to cure. [S]
Systemic therapy as below.
Restaging CT after three cycles.

Gallbladder adenocarcinoma, stage IVB (C23). ECOG 1, Child-Pugh A6, bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, creatinine 0.84 mg/dL (estimated creatinine clearance about 80 mL/min), neutrophils 4.9 x10^3/uL and platelets 318 x10^3/uL: fit for gemcitabine, cisplatin and durvalumab, the first-line regimen Dr. Choi and the tumor board recommend. Baseline TSH 1.9 and CA 19-9 498 U/mL. Genomic profiling is pending. He chose to start today. [S]
Cycle 1 day 1 today: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 with durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1, every 21 days, for up to 8 cycles, then durvalumab every 4 weeks.
Ondansetron at home for nausea.
Teaching on fever, infection and immune-related side effects; oncology line number given.
Restaging CT after three cycles.

Resolved hepatitis B infection (Z86.19). HBV DNA undetectable before treatment. [S]
HBV DNA and ALT in about 2 to 3 months.

Coping with a new diagnosis of advanced cancer. PHQ-9 6 (mild), with low mood and poor sleep since the result and no thoughts of self-harm; an expected reaction to grave news. Specialist palliative care starts now alongside treatment. [S]
First palliative care visit next week.
Sleep advice; review the PHQ-9 at the next visit.
